purpose: Human-supplied high-motion motorcycle continuity stress test at 480p15 using the fixed original 12-actual/8-forecast schedule.

scenarios.name: motorcycle_physics_480p15_seed82303
scenarios.prompt:
integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1]
Create a 15-second cinematic nighttime motorcycle chase through a dense modern city after rain. The same female rider and the same red sport motorcycle must remain visually consistent throughout the entire continuous shot.

0–3s: The camera travels backward directly in front of the motorcycle at nearly the same speed. The rider accelerates hard in a straight line through wet city traffic. Her torso leans slightly forward under acceleration. Hair, jacket fabric, and loose clothing react continuously to airflow. Road markings, reflections, streetlights, and surrounding vehicles move backward at physically consistent relative speeds.

3–6s: A white sedan ahead begins changing lanes and partially blocks the rider’s path. The rider first reduces speed slightly, then initiates a smooth evasive maneuver to the left. The motorcycle progressively leans left and follows a continuous curved trajectory around the sedan. There must be no instantaneous sideways movement, teleportation, sudden heading change, or unnatural drift. Steering angle, motorcycle lean, rider body lean, and path curvature remain physically connected.

6–10s: The camera drops close to wheel height and transitions into a fast three-quarter side tracking position. The rider accelerates again and passes through a narrow moving gap between two cars traveling in the same direction. For a brief moment, parts of the motorcycle and rider become occluded by the cars. When they reappear, their position, speed, direction, motorcycle geometry, rider identity, posture, and momentum remain continuous with the state before occlusion.

10–13s: The road enters a broad right-hand curve. The rider begins the turn before reaching the curve apex, smoothly leaning the motorcycle to the right. The tires maintain visible contact with the road surface. The motorcycle follows a natural curved path determined by its speed and lean angle. The rider gradually returns the motorcycle upright while exiting the turn. No sliding, floating, snapping, or impossible corrections.

13–15s: The camera arcs outward and upward behind the motorcycle while the rider continues accelerating away along the road. Traffic remains dynamically consistent around her. She maintains the same overall direction of travel and disappears deeper into the illuminated city.

Maintain continuous forward momentum throughout the sequence. No teleportation, sudden lateral displacement, instantaneous changes in velocity or direction, reversed movement, morphing, or object replacement. Wheel rotation remains consistent with vehicle speed. Tires stay attached to the road except for physically plausible suspension motion. Motorcycle lean corresponds to turning direction and path curvature. The rider reacts naturally to acceleration, braking, cornering, wind, road vibration, and minor bumps. Occlusion never resets position, pose, velocity, identity, or orientation. All surrounding cars maintain coherent trajectories and relative speeds.

Camera: Dynamic cinematic chase cinematography with continuous spatial logic, fast but readable movement, natural parallax, realistic relative-speed motion blur, and no impossible camera teleportation or arbitrary cuts.

Visual style: Photorealistic wet asphalt and reflections, dense nighttime urban lighting, high-detail motorcycle materials, realistic tire deformation and suspension response, and a strong sense of speed, mass, inertia, and momentum. No slow motion, fantasy physics, exaggerated drifting, morphing, subtitles, titles, or visible text.

overall_soundscape: Continuous synchronized red sport motorcycle engine acceleration and deceleration, realistic tire contact on wet asphalt, passing traffic, rainwater spray, airflow, suspension movement, and dense nighttime city ambience. No speech, voice, narration, chanting, or unintelligible human vocalization.
